contract.statement: For one-dimensional acoustics, let p(x,t) be the pressure perturbation and u(x,t) the particle velocity, with constant bulk modulus K and density ρ. The equations p_t + K u_x = 0 and u_t + (1/ρ)p_x = 0 are represented by q_t + A q_x = 0 when q is the column (p,u)^T and A has rows (0,K) and (1/ρ,0) [raw PDF page 24, equations (1.5)–(1.6) and intervening paragraph]. The inherited framework uses real variables and a constant real coefficient matrix, with subscripts denoting partial derivatives [raw PDF page 23, equation (1.1) and following paragraph]. The passage does not specify a regularity class or explicit parameter-sign assumptions; nonzero density is an inferred requirement of its ordinary reciprocal [raw PDF page 24, equations (1.5)–(1.6)].
assumptions: The scalar acoustic equations are p_t(x,t) + K u_x(x,t) = 0 and u_t(x,t) + (1/ρ)p_x(x,t) = 0 [raw PDF page 24, equation (1.5)].
K and ρ are constant for the displayed model [raw PDF page 24, paragraph identifying the material constants between (1.5) and (1.6)].

The partial derivatives appearing in the equations must be meaningful; no explicit differentiability class is supplied [raw PDF page 23, partial-derivative convention following (1.1); page 24, equation (1.5)].

The ordinary real reciprocal 1/ρ requires ρ ≠ 0. This is a mathematical domain requirement inferred from the displayed reciprocal, not an expressly stated hypothesis [raw PDF page 24, equations (1.5)–(1.6)].

The selected system belongs to the homogeneous, first-order, constant-coefficient linear framework in one spatial dimension [raw PDF page 23, introduction to (1.1); page 24, sentence preceding (1.6)].
The physical application is acoustic propagation in both directions through a one-dimensional medium [raw PDF page 24, paragraph introducing (1.5)].

Chapter 2 is cited as the location of the acoustic equations' derivation; the selected passage states the equations and their matrix representation directly [raw PDF page 24, sentence introducing (1.5)].
quantifiers: Inherited framework: x and t are real spatial and temporal variables, respectively [raw PDF page 23, equation (1.1) and q : R × R → R^m].

p and u are unknown real-valued functions of (x,t); the selected two-component state specializes the general framework to m = 2 [raw PDF page 24, equations (1.5)–(1.6); page 23, paragraph following (1.1)].

K and ρ are constant material parameters, with real coefficients inherited from the general system [raw PDF page 24, paragraph between (1.5) and (1.6); page 23, description of A as a constant real matrix].

The displayed equations concern the functions at general (x,t); no separate initial-value data, boundary data, or explicitly restricted space-time domain is specified [raw PDF page 24, equation (1.5) and its rewriting preceding (1.6)].
